factors.name: Supplier invoices are not matched to goods received
factors.description: Supplier invoices are approved and paid without being matched to goods received notes (GRNs) or other evidence that the goods or services were actually received.
factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where purchases are made on credit and a goods-receipt process exists or should exist.
factors.warning_signs: Invoices approved for payment without GRN references; GRNs not sequentially controlled; staff unable to locate receiving evidence for sampled invoices.
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factors.name: Goods received before year-end are invoiced afterward
factors.description: Goods or services are received before the reporting date, but the supplier invoice arrives (or is recorded) after the reporting date, so the liability and the purchase may be omitted from the current period.
factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where suppliers invoice in arrears or where invoice processing backlogs occur at period end.
factors.warning_signs: GRNs dated before year-end with no matching invoice at the reporting date; post-year-end invoices relating to pre-year-end receipts; weak or absent accrual procedures for uninvoiced receipts.
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factors.name: Supplier master records can be changed without independent approval
factors.description: Additions and changes to supplier master data - including bank details - can be made by the same person who processes payments, without independent authorisation.
factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where supplier payments are significant and master data controls who gets paid and into which account.
factors.warning_signs: No log of master changes; the same user creates suppliers and processes payments; changes to bank details shortly before large payments.
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factors.name: Duplicate invoices are processed
factors.description: The purchase system or manual processes allow the same supplier invoice to be recorded and paid more than once - for example, where invoice numbers are not validated for uniqueness per supplier.
factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where invoice volumes are high, where invoices arrive through multiple channels (email, post, portal), or where no automated duplicate check exists.
factors.warning_signs: Supplier statements showing credit balances; duplicate invoice numbers in the purchase ledger; suppliers querying double payments.
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factors.name: Purchases are recorded in an incorrect accounting period
factors.description: Purchases and the related payables are recorded by reference to the invoice date or processing date rather than the date the goods were received or the service performed, placing them in the wrong accounting period.
factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant at every period end, and especially where invoice processing lags goods receipt.
factors.warning_signs: Large invoices processed just after period end relating to earlier receipts; month-end purchase spikes driven by processing dates; cut-off errors found in prior periods.
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

risks.title: Invalid purchases recorded and paid for goods not received
risks.description: Purchases may be recorded - and paid - for goods or services never received. This is a potential misstatement and a possible control deficiency; the factor does not prove any invoice was invalid.
risks.causes: No matching of invoices to GRNs; weak segregation between ordering, receiving and payment approval; opportunity for fictitious invoices to be introduced.
risks.potential_consequences: Purchases and trade payables overstated; cash lost through payments for goods not received; duplicate or fictitious supplier payments.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with purchase volumes, manual approval processes and weak segregation of duties. An unmatched invoice is an exception to investigate, not a confirmed misstatement. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

risks.title: Unrecorded liabilities and understated purchases at the reporting date
risks.description: Goods received before year-end but invoiced afterward may be omitted from purchases and payables, understating liabilities. The factor describes a cut-off exposure; it does not prove any liability was omitted.
risks.causes: Invoices arriving after the reporting date; no accrual for unmatched GRNs; purchases recorded by invoice date rather than receipt date.
risks.potential_consequences: Trade payables and purchases understated; the subsequent period correspondingly overstated; incomplete liabilities affecting going-concern and covenant assessments.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Completeness of liabilities is inherently harder to test than existence, because the auditor looks for what is missing. The search for unrecorded liabilities is the standard response. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

risks.title: Payments to fictitious or altered suppliers; invalid payable balances
risks.description: Uncontrolled changes to supplier master data may divert payments to fictitious suppliers or altered bank accounts, and may create invalid payable balances. The control weakness is the finding; whether any payment was actually diverted requires investigation.
risks.causes: No independent approval of master changes; the same person maintains suppliers and processes payments; no periodic review of the supplier master.
risks.potential_consequences: Cash misappropriated through diverted payments; purchases overstated with fictitious invoices; payable balances owed to non-existent suppliers.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: This is both a control deficiency and a fraud opportunity. A change-log exception is a control deviation, not proof of fraud. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists or that fraud has occurred.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

risks.title: Duplicate recording of purchases and duplicate payments
risks.description: The same supplier invoice may be recorded twice, overstating purchases and payables, and may be paid twice, causing a cash loss. Duplication is usually error, but the factor must be tested rather than assumed.
risks.causes: No validation of invoice number uniqueness per supplier; invoices received through multiple channels; paid invoices not marked to prevent reprocessing.
risks.potential_consequences: Purchases and payables overstated; duplicate cash payments; supplier credit balances requiring recovery.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with invoice volumes and decentralised processing. A duplicated invoice number is an exception requiring investigation - it may be a genuine reissued invoice from the supplier rather than a double recording. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

risks.title: Cut-off misstatement of purchases and trade payables
risks.description: Purchases recorded in the wrong period misstate both purchases and payables at the reporting date. Cut-off errors can fall in either direction and are often error rather than fraud.
risks.causes: Recording by invoice or processing date instead of receipt date; period-end processing backlogs; weak cut-off procedures.
risks.potential_consequences: Purchases and payables misstated at the reporting date; distorted monthly trends; knock-on effects on inventory and cost of sales.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Cut-off testing in both directions is the standard response. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factor_risk.trigger_condition: Supplier invoices are approved and paid without being matched to goods received notes or equivalent evidence of receipt.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies to credit purchases where receipt should be evidenced. May be irrelevant for recurring service charges with no meaningful receipt event (for example, rent or utilities), where approval against the contract is the relevant control.
factor_risk.explanation: Matching the invoice to the GRN is what proves the entity received what it is paying for. Without that match, nothing stops an invoice for goods never delivered - whether through error or fictitious billing - from being recorded and paid. The risk is therefore that recorded purchases did not occur (occurrence) and are inaccurately stated (accuracy).
factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether any matching is performed at all, and by whom; the volume and value of invoices approved without matches; whether segregation exists between receiving and payment approval.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: the three-way match of order, receipt and invoice is the fundamental control over purchase validity.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factor_risk.trigger_condition: Goods or services are received before the reporting date, but the supplier invoice is recorded after the reporting date.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where suppliers invoice in arrears or processing backlogs exist. May be irrelevant where the entity accrues all unmatched GRNs at period end and the accrual process is reliable.
factor_risk.explanation: A liability exists when the goods are received, not when the invoice arrives. If nothing records that liability at the reporting date, both purchases and payables are understated: the completeness assertion for the purchase population and for the payables balance is at risk, and the transactions fall in the wrong period (cut-off).
factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether unmatched GRNs are accrued at period end; the typical invoice lag by supplier; the materiality of uninvoiced receipts.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: the search for unrecorded liabilities, including GRN-to-ledger tracing, is the standard completeness response.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factor_risk.trigger_condition: Supplier master additions and changes, including bank details, can be made without independent approval.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies wherever supplier payments are processed from master data. May be irrelevant where all master changes require independent approval and the change log is reviewed, or where payments are trivial.
factor_risk.explanation: Supplier master data decides who gets paid and into which account. If the person who processes payments can also create suppliers or change bank details, the opportunity exists to invent a supplier or redirect a genuine supplier's payments. Recorded purchases and payables may then include amounts that are not genuine obligations (occurrence, existence). An unapproved change is a control deviation to investigate - it is not proof that any payment was diverted.
factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Who can change master data and who processes payments; whether a change log exists; whether bank-detail changes are verified independently.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: independent control over vendor master changes is a recognised anti-fraud control over disbursements.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factor_risk.trigger_condition: The purchase process allows the same supplier invoice to be recorded more than once.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where invoice uniqueness is not enforced per supplier. May be irrelevant where the system blocks duplicate invoice numbers per supplier and paid invoices are marked, provided manual journals cannot bypass those checks.
factor_risk.explanation: A second recording of the same invoice does not represent a second purchase: the duplicate entry did not occur as an economic event (occurrence), and if paid, cash leaves the business for a liability that does not exist (accuracy of amounts). Duplicate invoice numbers still require investigation, because a supplier may genuinely reissue an invoice.
factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether the system validates invoice number uniqueness; how paid invoices are marked; whether manual journals bypass system checks.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: duplicate detection through data analysis and validation of invoice uniqueness are standard responses.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factor_risk.trigger_condition: Purchases are recorded by invoice or processing date rather than by the goods receipt or service performance date.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies at every period end where processing lags receipt. May be irrelevant where the system derives the posting date from the GRN date automatically and the derivation cannot be overridden without approval.
factor_risk.explanation: The accounting period for a purchase is determined by when the goods were received or the service performed. Recording by invoice or processing date shifts purchases across the reporting date in either direction, misstating purchases (cut-off) and leaving the recorded purchase population incomplete for the correct period (completeness).
factor_risk.additional_info_needed: How posting dates are determined; the lag between receipt and processing at period end; whether cut-off errors were found in prior periods.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: cut-off testing comparing invoice dates with goods receipt dates is the standard response.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

risk_assertions.why_relevant: Purchases recorded without evidence of receipt may not represent genuine purchases - the recorded transaction may not have occurred.
risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant for credit purchases where receipt should be evidenced.

risk_assertions.why_relevant: Without matching, invoiced quantities and prices are not checked against what was ordered and received, so recorded amounts may be inaccurate.
risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where prices or quantities vary, or where GRNs record actual quantities received.

risk_assertions.why_relevant: Purchases belonging to the current period (goods received before year-end) may be recorded in the next period.
The population of recorded purchases may be incomplete: goods received but not yet invoiced are missing from it.
risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where suppliers invoice in arrears.

risk_assertions.why_relevant: The trade payables balance may be incomplete if liabilities for goods received are not accrued at the reporting date.
risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant at the reporting date where unmatched GRNs exist.

risk_assertions.why_relevant: Payments or purchases recorded against fictitious or altered suppliers may not represent genuine business transactions.
risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where master changes lack independent approval.

risk_assertions.why_relevant: Payable balances recorded as owed to suppliers may not represent genuine obligations if the supplier is fictitious or the details were altered.
risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant for balances owed to recently added or changed suppliers.

risk_assertions.why_relevant: A duplicate recording does not represent a second, separate purchase - the second entry did not occur as an economic event.
risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where invoice uniqueness per supplier is not enforced.

risk_assertions.why_relevant: Duplicate payments mean cash paid exceeds the genuine liability; the amounts recorded exceed what is actually owed.
risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where duplicates have been paid rather than merely recorded.

risk_assertions.why_relevant: Purchases must be recorded in the period the goods were received or the service performed, not the period the invoice was processed.
Purchases of the current period that are processed late may be missing from the recorded population for that period.
risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where processing lags receipt around the reporting date.

controls.description: Supplier invoices are matched to the purchase order and goods received note (three-way match) before approval for payment.
controls.objective: Prevent payment for goods not received.
controls.responsible_role: Accounts payable staff, independent of receiving
controls.evidence_of_operation: Matched invoice packs; exception reports of invoices approved without a match.
controls.limitations: Collusion between receiving and payables staff defeats the match; does not detect overpricing agreed with a genuine supplier.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: An exception report of invoices approved without matching GRNs is reviewed independently each month.
controls.objective: Detect invoices paid without evidence of receipt.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Exception report with review sign-off and follow-up actions documented.
controls.limitations: Detective only - payment may already have been made; relies on the completeness of the matching data.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Goods received notes are sequentially controlled; at period end, unmatched GRNs are accrued as liabilities.
controls.objective: Ensure liabilities for goods received are recorded at the reporting date.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Sequential GRN register; accrual journals with supporting GRN listings; review sign-off.
controls.limitations: Does not detect goods received without a GRN being raised.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Purchases are recorded by reference to the goods receipt date, enforced by system posting rules or a period-end cut-off checklist.
controls.objective: Record purchases in the correct accounting period.
controls.frequency: Per transaction and at period end
controls.evidence_of_operation: Completed cut-off checklist; system configuration showing posting-date derivation.
controls.limitations: Manual checklists can be skipped; system rules can be overridden by privileged users.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: All additions and changes to supplier master data, including bank details, require independent approval before taking effect.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorised or fictitious suppliers entering the payment process.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Change log showing requestor, approver and timestamps; supporting supplier verification documents.
controls.limitations: The approver may not verify the change independently; does not prevent changes by privileged system users.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: The supplier master file is independently reviewed periodically for duplicate, dormant or suspicious entries.
controls.objective: Detect fictitious or inappropriate suppliers in the master data.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Review working papers with conclusions and follow-up on flagged suppliers.
controls.limitations: Judgemental; may not identify well-concealed fictitious suppliers.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: The purchase system rejects or flags duplicate invoice numbers for the same supplier automatically.
controls.objective: Prevent the same invoice being recorded twice.
controls.evidence_of_operation: System configuration; exception reports of blocked or flagged duplicates.
controls.limitations: Only checks invoice number per supplier - the same economic invoice with an altered number passes; manual journals may bypass the check.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Paid invoices are physically or systemically marked as paid and filed to prevent reprocessing.
controls.objective: Prevent paid invoices re-entering the payment process.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Marked invoice copies or system paid flags; controlled filing.
controls.limitations: Manual marking can be missed under volume pressure.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: A period-end cut-off checklist requires payables staff to record purchases by goods receipt date and to review post-period invoices for pre-period receipts.
controls.objective: Ensure purchases are recorded in the correct period.
controls.limitations: Checklist compliance is not self-proving; time pressure at period end reduces effectiveness.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Finance reviews supplier invoices recorded after the reporting date to identify goods received before year-end.
controls.objective: Detect cut-off errors in purchases after the reporting date.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Review working papers listing post-year-end invoices checked against GRN dates.
controls.limitations: Only covers invoiced items; uninvoiced receipts still depend on the GRN accrual.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

risk_controls.explanation: The three-way match is the direct preventive control: no receipt evidence, no payment.
Detects invoices that bypassed the matching control so they can be investigated.
The unmatched-GRN accrual is designed to capture exactly this exposure at period end.
Recording by receipt date removes the timing mismatch at source.
Independent approval directly addresses the factor: changes cannot take effect unilaterally.
Periodic review detects fictitious or suspicious suppliers that the approval control missed.
Automated duplicate detection prevents the same invoice number being recorded twice per supplier.
Marking invoices as paid stops them re-entering the payment process.
The cut-off checklist enforces receipt-date recording at the highest-risk point: period end.
Post-year-end invoice review detects cut-off errors that the checklist missed.

procedures.title: Vouch purchase invoices to goods received notes and purchase orders
procedures.objective: Verify that recorded purchases are supported by evidence of receipt.
steps: Select a sample of purchase invoices across the period.
For each, inspect the matched purchase order and goods received note.
Verify quantities, prices and supplier details agree across documents.
Investigate invoices with no matching GRN or with mismatched details.
procedures.population: Purchase invoices recorded in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Stratify by value; include a mix of suppliers; bias toward invoices approved without a visible match.
procedures.expected_result: Each sampled invoice is matched to a valid GRN and purchase order with consistent details.
procedures.exception_criteria: Invoices with no GRN; quantity or price mismatches; GRNs dated after the invoice without explanation.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate whether exceptions represent missing documents or invalid purchases; quantify potential overstatement; extend testing if a pattern emerges.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Reperform the three-way matching control
procedures.objective: Test whether the matching control operated effectively through the period.
steps: Select a sample of paid invoices.
Reperform the match: verify purchase order, GRN and invoice agreed before payment was released.
Note any payments released without a complete match.
Conclude on control operation.
procedures.population: Invoices subject to the matching control.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across the period; no deviations expected if reliance is planned.
procedures.exception_criteria: Payments released without a complete three-way match; evidence of override.
procedures.follow_up: A failed control test does not prove purchases are misstated - extend substantive vouching to establish whether invalid purchases were actually recorded; reassess control risk.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Inspect the unmatched-invoices exception report
procedures.objective: Verify that invoices paid without matching evidence were valid and followed up.
steps: Obtain the exception report of invoices approved without matching GRNs.
Inspect the independent review and follow-up documented.
For a sample of items, inspect the alternative evidence of receipt obtained.
Assess whether unresolved items indicate invalid purchases.
procedures.population: Exception report items for the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Focus on high-value and long-outstanding items.
procedures.expected_result: All exceptions were independently reviewed and resolved with valid evidence of receipt.
procedures.exception_criteria: Unreviewed exceptions; items cleared without evidence; long-outstanding unmatched invoices.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate unresolved items as potential invalid purchases; quantify exposure; consider implications for the control environment.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Trace pre-year-end goods received notes to the purchase ledger
procedures.objective: Detect liabilities for goods received but not recorded at year-end.
steps: Obtain the sequential GRN register for the window before the reporting date.
Select GRNs and trace each to the purchase ledger or the year-end accrual.
Verify the liability was recorded in the correct period.
List unmatched GRNs and agree them to accrual journals.
procedures.population: GRNs in the window before the reporting date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Focus on the final days before year-end and high-value receipts.
procedures.expected_result: All selected GRNs are recorded as purchases or accrued liabilities in the correct period.
procedures.exception_criteria: GRNs with no matching purchase or accrual; accruals unsupported by GRNs.
procedures.follow_up: Propose accrual adjustments for unrecorded liabilities; quantify the understatement; assess whether the accrual process needs extended testing.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Test post-year-end purchase invoices for pre-year-end receipt
procedures.objective: Verify that invoices recorded after year-end do not hide pre-year-end liabilities.
steps: Select purchase invoices recorded in the first weeks after the reporting date.
Inspect the related GRN dates.
Where goods were received before year-end, verify an accrual was recorded.
Aggregate with pre-year-end direction testing.
procedures.population: Purchase invoices recorded shortly after the reporting date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Cover at least two to four weeks after year-end.
procedures.expected_result: Post-year-end invoices relate to post-year-end receipts, or pre-year-end receipts were accrued.
procedures.exception_criteria: Invoices for pre-year-end receipts recorded only after year-end with no accrual.
procedures.follow_up: Propose cut-off adjustments; extend the post-year-end window if errors indicate a systematic problem.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Inspect the year-end accrual for unmatched goods received
procedures.objective: Verify that management's accrual for uninvoiced receipts is complete and supported.
steps: Obtain the year-end accrual schedule for unmatched GRNs.
Test the completeness of the GRN population used.
Agree a sample of accrued items to GRNs and subsequent invoices.
Assess whether the accrual basis (quantities, prices) is reasonable.
procedures.sampling_notes: Test the schedule as a whole; sample accrued items for agreement to GRNs.
procedures.expected_result: The accrual is complete, supported by GRNs and recorded at appropriate amounts.
procedures.exception_criteria: Incomplete GRN population; accrued items without GRN support; unreasonable pricing assumptions.
procedures.follow_up: Perform independent completeness testing where the schedule cannot be relied upon; propose adjustments for unsupported amounts.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Inspect the supplier master change log and approvals
procedures.objective: Test whether changes to supplier master data were independently approved.
steps: Obtain the supplier master change log for the period.
Select a sample of changes, including all changes to bank details.
Inspect evidence of independent approval and supporting verification.
Identify changes made by users who also process payments.
procedures.population: Supplier master changes in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of bank-detail changes; sample other changes.
procedures.expected_result: All sampled changes were independently approved with supporting verification documents.
procedures.exception_criteria: Unapproved changes; changes approved by the requestor; missing verification documents.
procedures.follow_up: Unapproved changes are control deviations, not proof of fraud: investigate the business reason, verify the supplier's legitimacy, and vouch related payments; extend testing if deviations are systemic.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Vouch payments to newly added or changed suppliers
procedures.objective: Verify that payments to new or changed suppliers relate to genuine business transactions.
steps: Identify suppliers added or changed during the period.
Select payments made to those suppliers.
Vouch each payment to the purchase order, GRN and invoice.
Verify the supplier's legitimacy through independent evidence (for example, business registration or verified contact details).
procedures.population: Payments to suppliers added or changed in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Bias toward suppliers with limited trading history and large first payments.
procedures.expected_result: Payments are supported by genuine purchase documentation and the supplier is independently verifiable.
procedures.exception_criteria: Payments without supporting purchase evidence; suppliers that cannot be independently verified.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate unverifiable suppliers thoroughly; trace the flow of funds where possible; if diversion is suspected, treat as a fraud indicator and consider the need for forensic expertise - do not conclude fraud has occurred.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Analyse the supplier master for indicators of fictitious suppliers
procedures.objective: Detect anomalies in supplier master data suggesting fictitious entries.
steps: Obtain the full supplier master file.
Analyse for duplicate bank accounts, duplicate addresses, PO box addresses, and suppliers sharing employee addresses or contact details.
Flag suppliers with no purchase history but with payments, and round-sum payment patterns.
Investigate flagged suppliers with corroborating evidence.
procedures.sampling_notes: Full-population analysis; judgemental investigation of flagged items.
procedures.expected_result: Flagged items are explained by genuine business reasons with supporting evidence.
procedures.exception_criteria: Multiple suppliers sharing bank details; suppliers unverifiable through independent sources.
procedures.follow_up: Subject flagged suppliers to detailed vouching and verification; treat persistent anomalies as fraud risk indicators.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Use data analysis to identify potential duplicate invoices
procedures.objective: Detect invoices that may have been recorded more than once.
steps: Obtain the full purchase ledger for the period.
Analyse for duplicate combinations of supplier, invoice number, date and amount, and for near-duplicates with altered invoice numbers.
Select potential duplicates for detailed testing.
Distinguish genuine reissued invoices from double recordings.
procedures.expected_result: Potential duplicates are explained (for example, genuine reissued invoices with credit notes) or confirmed as isolated errors.
procedures.exception_criteria: Confirmed double recordings; duplicate payments identified.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify double-recorded purchases and duplicate payments; investigate the control breakdown; propose adjustments and recovery of duplicate payments.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Vouch suspected duplicate invoices to invoice copies and payment records
procedures.objective: Establish whether suspected duplicates are genuine double recordings.
steps: For each suspected duplicate, obtain the supplier invoice copies.
Compare invoice numbers, dates, amounts and supporting GRNs.
Inspect payment records to determine whether both entries were paid.
Conclude whether a duplicate recording or duplicate payment occurred.
procedures.population: Suspected duplicate invoices flagged by data analysis.
procedures.sampling_notes: All flagged items above a de minimis threshold.
procedures.expected_result: Each suspected duplicate is resolved: either a genuine separate invoice or a confirmed duplicate with quantified effect.
procedures.exception_criteria: Confirmed duplicate recordings; duplicate payments made.
procedures.follow_up: Propose adjustments for overstated purchases and payables; follow up on recovery of duplicate payments from suppliers.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Inspect whether paid invoices are marked to prevent reprocessing
procedures.objective: Test the control preventing paid invoices re-entering the payment process.
steps: Select a sample of paid invoices.
Inspect whether each is marked as paid (stamp, system flag) and filed appropriately.
Consider whether any paid invoice could be reprocessed.
Conclude on control operation.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across the period and across processing staff.
procedures.expected_result: Paid invoices are consistently marked and controlled against reprocessing.
procedures.exception_criteria: Unmarked paid invoices; invoices accessible for reprocessing.
procedures.follow_up: Where the control fails, extend substantive duplicate testing; a failed control test alone does not prove duplicates exist.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Test purchase cut-off around the reporting date
procedures.objective: Verify purchases are recorded in the period the goods were received.
steps: Select purchase invoices from the last days before and first days after the reporting date.
Compare invoice dates with GRN dates.
Select GRNs from the same window and trace to the purchase ledger.
Investigate items where invoice and receipt dates fall in different periods.
procedures.population: Purchase invoices and GRNs around the reporting date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Both directions; extend the window if processing backlogs exist.
procedures.expected_result: Purchases are recorded in the period of receipt; no material cut-off errors.
procedures.exception_criteria: Purchases recorded by invoice date in a different period from receipt.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify cut-off errors and propose adjustments; if systematic, extend testing and reassess the period-end process.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Trace goods received notes to the purchase ledger for completeness
procedures.objective: Verify that all goods received are recorded as purchases.
steps: Select GRNs from across the period, with emphasis on period end.
Trace each to the purchase ledger.
Verify quantities and amounts recorded agree with the GRN.
Follow up on GRNs with no matching purchase.
procedures.sampling_notes: Emphasis on period end; include high-value receipts.
procedures.expected_result: All selected GRNs are recorded completely and accurately.
procedures.exception_criteria: GRNs with no matching purchase; quantity or amount differences.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate unrecorded GRNs; propose adjustments; consider whether the pattern indicates a completeness problem requiring extended procedures.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedures.title: Analyse monthly purchase trends for cut-off anomalies
procedures.objective: Identify unusual purchase patterns suggesting cut-off errors.
steps: Compare monthly purchases and payables with prior periods and budgets.
Investigate months with unusual spikes or troughs, especially around period ends.
Correlate with inventory movements and operational data.
Corroborate explanations with documentary evidence.
procedures.population: Monthly purchase data for the period.
procedures.expected_result: Trends are consistent with operational activity; variances explained and corroborated.
procedures.exception_criteria: Unexplained period-end spikes or troughs inconsistent with operations.
procedures.follow_up: Direct cut-off testing at the months flagged; analytical exceptions alone are not misstatements.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

risk_procedures.reason: Core validity test: ties each recorded purchase to evidence of receipt.
Tests the three-way match control directly; failure redirects to extended vouching.
Follows up the population most at risk: invoices paid without matching evidence.
GRN-to-ledger tracing is the completeness direction for unrecorded liabilities.
Post-year-end invoices are where pre-year-end liabilities hide.
Tests management's own accrual before relying on it.
Tests the independent-approval control over master changes directly.
Payments to new or changed suppliers are the highest-risk disbursements.
Full-population analysis catches fictitious suppliers that targeted testing might miss.
Data analysis across the full ledger is the efficient way to find duplicates.
Resolves each suspected duplicate with documentary evidence.
Tests the preventive control against reprocessing paid invoices.
Two-directional cut-off testing catches misstatements in either direction.
GRN tracing tests completeness of the purchase population.
Trend analysis directs cut-off testing to the months most at risk.

evidence.name: Supplier invoices
evidence.description: Supplier invoices recorded in the period, with purchase order references where available.
evidence.reliability_notes: Received documents, but reliability as evidence of a genuine purchase depends on matching to independent receipt evidence. An invoice proves a claim was made, not that goods were received.
evidence.limitations: Does not by itself prove receipt or correct timing.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Supplier details; unique invoice numbers; dates; quantities and prices.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: GRNs showing different quantities; supplier statements disputing the invoice.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Goods received notes
evidence.description: Goods received notes recording quantities received, dates and receiving staff.
evidence.reliability_notes: More reliable where GRNs are sequentially controlled and prepared by staff independent of purchasing and payables; the GRN is the primary evidence that receipt occurred.
evidence.limitations: Only evidences recorded receipts; collusion at the receiving point undermines reliability.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Sequential numbering; receipt dates; quantities; receiver identification.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Invoices for quantities exceeding the GRN; GRNs dated after the invoice without explanation.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Purchase orders and matching records
evidence.description: Approved purchase orders and the matching records showing order, GRN and invoice agreement before payment.
evidence.reliability_notes: Purchase orders evidence authorisation; matching records show the control operated. Reliability depends on segregation between ordering, receiving and payment functions.
evidence.limitations: An order proves authorisation, not receipt; matching records can be completed perfunctorily.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Authorised orders; complete three-way agreement before payment release.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Payments released without a complete match.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Goods received notes around year-end
evidence.description: Sequential GRN register for the period straddling the reporting date.
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on sequential control of the GRN register; the register is the population for completeness testing of liabilities.
evidence.limitations: Goods received without a GRN being raised leave no trace.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete sequence with no unexplained gaps around year-end.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Gaps in sequence; GRNs with no matching purchase or accrual.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Purchase ledger extracts after year-end
evidence.description: Purchase ledger extracts for the weeks following the reporting date.
evidence.reliability_notes: System-generated extracts are reliable as to what was recorded and when; they cannot show liabilities that were omitted.
evidence.limitations: Recording date may differ from the receipt date that determines the correct period.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete extraction; reconciled totals to the general ledger.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: GRN dates contradicting the recorded period.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Year-end accrual schedules for unmatched GRNs
evidence.description: Management's schedule accruing liabilities for goods received but not invoiced at the reporting date.
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on the completeness of the GRN population used and the reasonableness of pricing; auditor reperformance of the schedule increases assurance.
evidence.limitations: A schedule proves arithmetic, not completeness of inputs.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Reconciled to the GRN register; reasonable pricing basis; reviewed and signed off.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Accrued items without GRN support; GRNs omitted from the schedule.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Supplier master change log
evidence.description: System log of additions and changes to supplier master data, including bank details, with user and timestamp.
evidence.reliability_notes: System-generated logs are more reliable than manual records; reliability depends on restricted access to the master file and on the log being tamper-evident.
evidence.limitations: Shows that a change was made, not whether it was legitimate.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete chronological record; requestor and approver identified.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Changes with no approval record; changes by users who also process payments.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Approval records for supplier master changes
evidence.description: Documented independent approvals for supplier master additions and changes, with supporting verification.
evidence.reliability_notes: Evidences that an approval step occurred; reliability as evidence of legitimacy depends on whether the approver verified the change independently.
evidence.limitations: Does not prove the approver checked the underlying supplier details.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Independent approver; dated; supporting verification documents attached.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Approvals by the requestor; missing verification documents.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Supplier verification documents and payment records
evidence.description: Independent evidence of supplier legitimacy (business registration, verified contact and bank details) and the related payment records.
evidence.reliability_notes: Independent verification, such as a business register extract or bank-confirmed account details, is more reliable than documents supplied by the payee. Payment records show where the money actually went.
evidence.limitations: Verification is point-in-time; details may change after verification.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Independently sourced; consistent with the master data and payment destination.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Payments to accounts differing from verified details; unverifiable suppliers.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Purchase ledger data extracts
evidence.description: Complete purchase ledger data for the period, used for duplicate analysis.
evidence.reliability_notes: Complete system extracts are reliable for data analysis; the analysis is only as good as the underlying data.
evidence.limitations: Analysis finds patterns, not conclusions; each flagged item needs investigation.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Control totals that do not reconcile to the general ledger.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Supplier invoice copies and payment records
evidence.description: Copies of supplier invoices for suspected duplicates and the related payment records showing what was paid and when.
evidence.reliability_notes: Invoice copies obtained from the supplier corroborate the recorded invoice; payment records establish whether duplicates were actually paid, which determines the financial effect.
evidence.limitations: A supplier may reissue an invoice legitimately; copies alone do not distinguish this from double recording.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Matched invoice numbers, dates and amounts; payment records reconciled to bank.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Two payments for one invoice; credit notes not recorded.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Duplicate detection exception reports
evidence.description: System reports of blocked or flagged potential duplicate invoices.
evidence.reliability_notes: System-generated reports are reliable as to what the system flagged; the auditor must still assess what the system's logic cannot flag, such as altered invoice numbers.
evidence.limitations: Only as good as the detection logic; manual journals may bypass it.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete flagging log; documented follow-up on each flagged item.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Confirmed duplicates that the system did not flag.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Purchase invoices with posting and receipt dates
evidence.description: Purchase invoices around the reporting date showing both the invoice date and the related goods receipt date.
evidence.reliability_notes: Comparison of invoice dates with GRN dates is the core cut-off evidence; reliability depends on both dates being genuine and independently recorded.
evidence.limitations: Either date can be manipulated; corroboration across documents matters.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Both dates present and consistent with supporting GRNs.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: GRN dates in a different period from the posting date.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Period-end cut-off working papers
evidence.description: Management's cut-off checklist and the auditor's cut-off testing working papers.
evidence.reliability_notes: Auditor-prepared working papers documenting cut-off testing are highly reliable as evidence of the work performed; a client checklist evidences that a process was followed, not its outcome.
evidence.limitations: A completed checklist does not prove the underlying testing was effective.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Signed off; complete coverage of the cut-off window; conclusions documented.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Cut-off errors found despite a completed checklist.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.name: Monthly purchase reports and budgets
evidence.description: Monthly purchase reports compared with budgets and prior periods.
evidence.reliability_notes: Useful for identifying anomalies that direct testing; reliability as audit evidence is limited - trends support risk assessment rather than proving individual transactions.
evidence.limitations: Not evidence of individual transactions; budgets may be unreliable.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Consistent basis of preparation across periods.
evidence.contradictory_evidence: Unexplained variances that management cannot corroborate.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

procedure_evidence.notes: Invoices are the population vouched.
GRNs are inspected for each sampled invoice.
Matching records are what the control is reperformed on.
Exception items are followed up to alternative receipt evidence.
GRN register is the population traced.
Accrual journals are traced to for unmatched GRNs.
Post-year-end invoices are the population tested.
GRN dates establish the true receipt period.
The accrual schedule is directly inspected.
GRN register tests the schedule's input completeness.
Change log is the population inspected.
Approval records evidence the control.
Verification documents and payment records are the core evidence.
GRNs support the genuineness of the underlying purchase.
Change log and master data are analysed.
Ledger extracts are the analysed population.
System flags are compared with the auditor's analysis.
Invoice copies and payment records resolve each suspected duplicate.
Paid invoices are inspected for paid markings.
Invoice and receipt dates are compared.
Cut-off working papers document the testing.
GRNs are the population traced.
Monthly reports provide the trend data.

rules.name: Unmatched supplier invoices -> invalid purchase risk

missing_information: Whether any matching is performed at all, and by whom.
The volume and value of invoices approved without matches.
Whether segregation exists between receiving and payment approval.
then.note: An unmatched invoice is an exception to investigate, not a confirmed invalid purchase.

rules.rationale: Without matching to receipt evidence, nothing stops invoices for goods never delivered from being recorded and paid. The rule directs vouching to GRNs, a test of the matching control, and follow-up of the exception population most at risk.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

rules.name: Late supplier invoices -> unrecorded liabilities risk

missing_information: Whether unmatched GRNs are accrued at period end.
The typical invoice lag by supplier.
then.note: Completeness of liabilities is tested by looking for what is missing: GRN-to-ledger tracing is the key procedure.

rules.rationale: A liability exists on receipt, not on invoicing; late invoices therefore create unrecorded liabilities. The rule directs two-directional cut-off testing around GRNs and inspection of management's accrual, targeting completeness and cut-off.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

rules.name: Uncontrolled supplier master changes -> fictitious supplier risk

missing_information: Who can change master data and who processes payments.
Whether a tamper-evident change log exists.
Whether bank-detail changes are verified independently.
then.note: An unapproved change is a control deviation to investigate - it is not proof that any payment was diverted or that fraud occurred.

rules.rationale: Master data decides who gets paid and into which account, so uncontrolled changes create both error and fraud opportunity. The rule directs a test of the approval control, substantive vouching of payments to new or changed suppliers, and full-population analysis for fictitious-supplier indicators.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

rules.name: Duplicate invoice processing -> duplicate recording risk

missing_information: Whether the system validates invoice number uniqueness per supplier.
How paid invoices are marked against reprocessing.
Whether manual journals bypass system checks.
then.note: A duplicate invoice number still requires investigation: the supplier may have genuinely reissued the invoice.

rules.rationale: A second recording of the same invoice is not a second purchase, and a second payment is a cash loss. The rule directs full-population duplicate analysis, documentary resolution of each suspected duplicate, and a test of the paid-invoice control.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

rules.name: Wrong-period purchase recording -> cut-off risk

missing_information: How posting dates are determined (receipt date vs invoice date).
The lag between receipt and processing at period end.
Whether cut-off errors were found in prior periods.
then.note: Cut-off errors can fall in either direction and are often error rather than fraud; testing covers both directions.

rules.rationale: The correct period for a purchase is determined by receipt, not by invoice processing. The rule directs two-directional cut-off testing, GRN tracing for completeness, and trend analysis to focus testing on the months most at risk.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
